newsitem.title: INDIA: Slow demand weighs on Indian sub-continent gold.
newsitem.headline: Slow demand weighs on Indian sub-continent gold.

text.p: Slow wedding season demand and weak world markets will continue to weigh down Indian sub-continent gold prices this week, dealers said on Monday.
"Demand for the wedding season remained lower than expected while higher supplies pushed prices downward," said Mahavir Shah," a Bombay bullion dealer.
India's traditional wedding season lasts for about three months, beginning end-November.
Gold prices fell 30 rupees per 10 grams to 5,010 rupees on the Bombay Bullion Exchange in the week to Monday.

Shah said traders expected a further drop in demand for gold in the coming days because of the onset of a month-long inauspicious period which, as indicated by a Hindu calendar, will last till mid-January.
"I expect fresh buying only in January," he said.
In Karachi gold gained 142 rupees per 10 grams in the week to Sunday, but dealers in Pakistan expect prices to fall in the next few days because of a cash crunch.
Dealers said consumers were holding on to their cash due to political uncertainty ahead of national elections scheduled for February 3, 1997.
They said there had been a steep fall in demand for jewellery even though the wedding season is in a full swing.
"There are 40 percent less buyers of jewellery this year compared to last year," said Saeed Qureshi, a member of the All Pakistan Gem and Jewellers' Association.
In Dubai, key Indian demand for gold has yet to take off despite a favourable mix of falling prices and the Indian marriage season, bullion traders said on Sunday.
After suffering from lacklustre demand during last month's Diwali (light) festival, souk traders are still waiting for wedding demand to turn around fourth quarter business.
"1996 has already gone. We are now looking at the market for 1997," said one trader who saw little scope for wedding demand to rally the market for the remainder of the year.
Much of Dubai's demand originates in India and Pakistan.
GOLD PRICES 24 CARATS PER 10 GRAMMES IN U.S. DOLLARS
(Conversion $1=35.82 Indian rupees, 40.22 Pakistani rupees and 3.67 UAE Dirhams)
* Bombay prices December 16 & 9, Karachi and Dubai prices December 15 & 8 respectively.
